plan.contextChunk: This figure places three small sketched graphs side by side, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing curves that rise from left to right on an unmarked vertical axis above a horizontal axis whose tip is labeled n; no numeric ticks appear anywhere. Panel (a) carries three curves: the highest is labeled c2 g(n), the lowest c1 g(n), and a third labeled f(n) weaves between them, dipping and crossing near the left edge before settling into the corridor between the other two. A dashed vertical segment drops from that crossing region to a tick on the n axis marked n0, and the expression f(n) = Theta(g(n)) is printed below the plot. Panel (b) has two curves, the upper labeled c g(n) and the lower labeled f(n); f(n) oscillates sharply at small n, meets c g(n) at the dashed line standing over the tick n0, and runs beneath it from there on, with f(n) = O(g(n)) underneath. Panel (c) reverses the roles, putting f(n) above and c g(n) below after they touch at the dashed n0 line, and is captioned f(n) = Omega(g(n)). Read against one another, the three panels turn on where the labeled curve sits relative to the scaled comparison function once n passes n0, giving the geometric intuition behind bounding a function from both sides, from above only, and from below only.

interactions.label: Threshold n0
interactions.teaches: Asymptotic bounds only have to hold for n ≥ n0, so the threshold can be placed past any finite region of messy early behavior — wiggles before n0 never disqualify the bound

interactions.label: Constant multiplier c
interactions.teaches: The bound curve is a constant rescaling of g(n): in Θ the corridor c1 g(n) to c2 g(n) widens or narrows (c1 = 1/c, c2 = c), in O the ceiling c g(n) rises or falls, in Ω the floor c g(n) rises or falls — the notation only requires that some constant works, which is why constant factors are ignored

interactions.label: Notation
interactions.teaches: Θ constrains f(n) from both sides at once, O only caps it from above, and Ω only floors it from below — the shaded permitted region makes the one-sided versus two-sided difference visible

demo_steps.title: Θ: a two-sided corridor
demo_steps.narration: In panel (a), f(n) is sandwiched between c1 g(n) and c2 g(n) for all n ≥ n0; the shaded corridor is the region f(n) must stay in once n passes the dashed line.

demo_steps.title: Push n0 into the messy region
demo_steps.narration: Drag n0 left and red violation marks appear where the early oscillations of f(n) escape the corridor — showing that bounds fail if the threshold is set before the function settles down.

demo_steps.title: Constants are negotiable
demo_steps.narration: Widening the multiplier restores the bound even at that early n0: any sufficiently large c2 (and small c1) works, which is exactly why asymptotic notation absorbs constant factors.

demo_steps.title: O: an upper ceiling only
demo_steps.narration: Panel (b) shades everything below c g(n): f(n) may dip far under the ceiling and still satisfy O — only escaping above it to the right of n0 counts as a violation.

demo_steps.title: Ω: a lower floor only
demo_steps.narration: Panel (c) flips the comparison: with c < 1, c g(n) is a floor and f(n) may soar arbitrarily above it — only dipping below the floor past n0 violates Ω.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Θ, O, and Ω each promise only that some constant multiple of g(n) bounds f(n) from the relevant side(s) for all n past some threshold n0 — constant factors and any finite amount of early misbehavior are simply ignored.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three small sketch-style graphs side by side on a white background, mirroring CLRS Figure 3.1: thin black hand-drawn curves, L-shaped axes with no numeric ticks, an arrow-tipped horizontal axis labeled n, italic serif math labels (c2 g(n), c1 g(n), f(n), c g(n)), a dashed vertical line dropping to a tick labeled n0, the caption equation centered beneath each panel, and the panel tag (a)/(b)/(c) below that. Curves rise left to right; f(n) has small wiggles near the left edge in every panel and settles into its bounded position right of the crossing point. In Θ view the slider c sets c2 = c and c1 = 1/c so the corridor scales symmetrically about g(n); in O view c scales the ceiling; in Ω view c scales the floor (use c < 1 there so the floor sits below f(n)). The active panel is full-contrast with its permitted region shaded translucent (corridor for Θ, area under the ceiling for O, area above the floor for Ω, shading applied only for n ≥ n0); inactive panels are dimmed but still visible. Wherever f(n) exits the permitted region to the right of n0, mark that segment in red. Animate dashed-line movement and shading smoothly as sliders change.
